purpose: Test whether the frozen ABM v4 isolation/opportunity mechanism transfers from coarse network size (Tier-A) to weighted interaction architecture (Tier-B) using original quantitative network sources without forcing them into a single Doré filtering pipeline.
prospective_status: Azores and Canary weighted values were already recovered before this registry; Mauritius and Seychelles source recovery, ABM Tier-B observation mapping, cross-system fit and all model-comparison decisions below are fixed before inspecting Mauritius/Seychelles weighted Tier-B values.
independent_system_unit: named oceanic-island archipelago/study system; nested sites/seasons do not increase independent system n

systems.source: Olesen et al. 2002 / IWDB Flores frequency matrix

systems.network_unit: five preregistered island aggregations: El Hierro, La Gomera, Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura, Tenerife

systems.source: Kaiser-Bunbury et al. 2009 / Interaction Web Database
systems.network_unit: source-defined invaded/control and restored heathland networks; source design determines whether they are analyzed separately or as a transparently declared aggregate

systems.source: Kaiser-Bunbury et al. 2017 restoration networks / original public interaction source
systems.network_unit: source-defined restoration/control site-time networks; nested observations are clustered within Seychelles

source_admission_rules: Interaction weights must be explicitly provided by the original/public quantitative source (visit counts, visitation frequency/rate, or another source-defined nonnegative interaction intensity).
A topology-only database is insufficient for weighted Tier-B and must not be converted into pseudo-counts from repeated rows.
Source-defined aggregation/grouping is fixed from methods/site identity before inspecting Tier-B metric fit.
Mismatch to Doré filtered aggregates does not trigger post-hoc deletion or regrouping; such systems remain source-native rather than Doré-identical.
Missing source delivery is not biological zero and excludes only that network from the quantitative layer.

interaction_diversity.metric: Shannon entropy of all positive source interaction weights normalized by total weight

plant_niche_overlap.metric: mean pairwise Morisita-Horn overlap among plant pollinator-weight vectors

abm_observation_mapping_to_freeze_before.interaction_weights: derive a nonnegative plant-by-pollinator opportunity matrix from the frozen v4 encounter/service process under the fixed total visit-budget interpretation; normalization may remove arbitrary total scale but may not use empirical Tier-B outcomes
abm_observation_mapping_to_freeze_before.interaction_diversity: apply the same Shannon formula as empirical networks to ABM pair weights
abm_observation_mapping_to_freeze_before.plant_niche_overlap: apply the same Morisita-Horn formula as empirical networks to ABM plant-by-pollinator weight vectors
abm_observation_mapping_to_freeze_before.posthoc_rule: all saturation values are reported; no preferred saturation may be selected from Tier-B fit

geography.primary: same GIFT nearest-mainland distance ECDF mapping fixed in Tier-A
geography.secondary: same geography-only PC1 sensitivity where all required fields are available

validation_design.primary_holdout: leave one whole named system out
validation_design.nested_rows: sites/islands/seasons within a system may contribute observations but the full system is withheld together
validation_design.baseline_1: source-size/sampling-design baseline using only prespecified observation-design/topology-size covariates available without Tier-B metric values
validation_design.baseline_2: nonmechanistic geography plus the same source-size/sampling layer
validation_design.mechanistic_model: ABM Tier-B feature plus the same source-size/sampling layer
validation_design.reporting: absolute prediction error and system-level fold results for every saturation; do not select systems by fit

success_rule: A mechanistic predictive-gain claim requires the ABM model to outperform the nonmechanistic geography baseline for the same target in at least 4 of 5 saturation settings, with no system replacement. Target-specific success/failure is reported separately; one target cannot rescue the other.
anti_overclaim: Source-native weighted systems are not called the same Doré estimand unless exact filtering reconciliation is independently demonstrated.
Visitation weights are not pollinator effectiveness or reproductive success.
Four systems support a first cross-system transfer test, not a universal global prevalence estimate.
Failure of Tier-B does not erase Tier-A predictive gain; it limits transfer from network size to weighted architecture.
